content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Write the equations for anaerobic respiration in animals and plants/yeast
Describe the consequences of anaerobic respiration

occurs without oxygen. It releases energy from glucose but produces different products and much less energy than aerobic respiration. It's used when oxygen supply is insufficient, such as during intense exercise.
Lactic acid builds up in muscles

content.text: Anaerobic Respiration in Plants and Yeast
Ethanol is toxic at high levels
Energy still trapped in lactic acid/ethanol
Only a fraction of potential energy released
Heart and lungs can't supply enough O₂
Blood carries lactic acid to liver
Liver converts lactic acid back to glucose

content.text: Anaerobic respiration only happens in microorganisms
Human muscles use it during intense exercise
Lactic acid is bad and should be avoided
It's a normal response to oxygen shortage and is recycled
Yeast dies when it respires anaerobically
Yeast thrives anaerobically (though ethanol eventually kills it)
Anaerobic respiration doesn't release any energy
It releases some energy, just much less than aerobic
Product of anaerobic respiration in animals
Alcohol produced by anaerobic respiration in yeast/plants
Tiredness due to lactic acid build-up
Extra oxygen needed to remove lactic acid
In animals: glucose → lactic acid + energy
In yeast/plants: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide + energy
Produces much less energy than aerobic respiration
Lactic acid causes muscle fatigue during exercise
Lactic acid is transported to liver for conversion back to glucose
Fermentation is used in brewing, baking, and biofuel production
Less efficient because glucose is not fully broken down
